title: A timeframe preset change refetches every tile and chart with the same boundary and updates the as-of stamp
asA: operator changing the dashboard timeframe from last-7-days to last-30-days
iWant: every tile and chart to refetch with the same from and to boundary and the same preset name
soThat: the shell renders a coherent snapshot at one boundary and the as-of stamp reads the same on every tile

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard surface and an operator-driven timeframe preset change (click a preset control, or select a value from a timeframe menu), one refetch fires per tile and one per rendered chart; every fetch carries the same `from` boundary, the same `to` boundary and the same `preset` name in its query string; once every fetch has returned (or the timeout has elapsed) the shell updates one `data-as-of` attribute on the shell root and every tile carries the same `data-as-of` value in ISO-8601 form. Probed by the application-dashboard pack check AC-19104-1 (Playwright drives to the dashboard route, waits for the initial fetch batch, clicks the second preset control, waits for the new batch, reads the request log from `window.__dashboardFetches` and from `GET /__requests`, and asserts every fetch in the new batch carries the same from/to/preset trio and every tile carries the same `data-as-of` matching the shell root).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard surface and a timeframe preset change
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request log and the DOM are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: every refetch carries the same from/to/preset and every tile's data-as-of matches the shell root

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard with an operator-elicited auto-refresh interval (ADR-2002), the shell refetches on the same fan-out contract at the interval: every tile refetches with the same from/to/preset, the as-of stamp updates on the shell root and every tile. When no auto-refresh interval is elicited, the shell does not refresh unattended (a dashboard that refreshes every ten seconds without an operator opt-in is a defect). The pack asserts the initial default is auto-refresh off through a `data-auto-refresh` attribute on the shell root; a fixture whose default is on fails project-side check. Applying agent sets: the elicited auto-refresh interval value in seconds (ADR-2002) or the explicit off default, recorded on the manifest and reflected on the shell root as `data-auto-refresh`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard with or without an elicited auto-refresh interval
acceptanceCriteria.then: auto-refresh is off unless the interval is elicited; refreshes follow the same fan-out contract

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard mid-refetch (a preset change fired 200ms ago; some tile fetches have returned, others are pending), when the operator activates a SECOND preset change, the shell cancels the in-flight fetches for the first preset and issues a fresh fan-out for the second preset; the pack asserts no tile renders data from the abandoned preset alongside data from the new one.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator activating a second preset change while the first fan-out is still in flight
acceptanceCriteria.when: the shell handles the second change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the in-flight first-preset fetches are cancelled and a fresh fan-out issues for the second preset; no mixed-preset data appears on tiles

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a preset change that fires a fan-out and every tile's fetch rejects (a network partition, a downstream outage), when every fetch has settled as a failure, then the shared `as of <ISO-8601>` stamp still advances (settled includes failed), every tile enters the error state carrying the shared stamp, and one aria-live polite announcement names the whole-surface failure so the operator hears the state change.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a preset change fan-out where every tile fetch rejects
acceptanceCriteria.when: every fetch has settled as a failure
acceptanceCriteria.then: the shared as-of stamp advances, every tile is in the error state carrying the shared stamp, and one aria-live announcement names the whole-surface failure

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard whose elicited timeframe presets include an operator-authored addition (per the elicited `timeframe-presets`), when the operator activates the elicited preset, the fan-out contract fires unchanged (same from/to/preset boundary on every fetch); a preset that fails to fire the fan-out because the shell does not recognise the elicited name fails the pack check. Applying agent sets: the elicited preset tokens.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator-elicited additional timeframe preset activated on the dashboard
acceptanceCriteria.then: the fan-out fires with the elicited preset name unchanged; a shell that ignores the elicited preset fails
